definition: A web standard that allows websites to control which browser features and APIs can be used by the site itself and any embedded third-party content like ads or widgets.
metaDescription: Learn about Permissions Policy - a web security feature that controls browser API access for websites and third-party content to protect user privacy.
simpleExplanation: Think of it as a bouncer for your web browser. When you visit a website, Permissions Policy decides what the site can and cannot do - like access your camera, location, or microphone. It also controls what embedded ads or widgets can do.
whyItMatters: It protects your privacy by preventing websites and third-party content from secretly accessing sensitive browser features. Without it, a malicious ad could potentially access your camera or location without your knowledge.
technicalDetail: Implemented through HTTP headers or HTML meta tags, Permissions Policy uses allowlists to specify which origins can use specific browser APIs. It replaces the older Feature Policy standard and provides granular control over features like geolocation, camera, microphone, and payment APIs.

examples.explanation: A news website sets a policy to block all camera access for embedded ads, preventing advertisers from secretly activating your webcam while you read articles.
An e-commerce site allows location access for its own store locator but blocks it for embedded customer review widgets that don't need your location.
A social platform permits microphone access for its own voice messaging feature but denies it to embedded third-party games or advertisements.
